  module V1
    class AccountsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_account!, only: %i[show cancel reactivate]
      before_action :authenticate_user!, only: %i[show cancel reactivate]
      before_action :require_active_account!, only: %i[show]
      before_action :require_owner!, only: %i[cancel reactivate]

      def create
        account_params = require_hash_param(:account)
        admin_raw = account_params[:admin]

        unless admin_raw.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || admin_raw.is_a?(Hash)
          return render json: {
            error: "Admin parameters are required",
            errors: { admin: [ "is required" ] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        account = Account.new(
          name: account_params[:name],
          subdomain: account_params[:subdomain]
        )
        user = User.new(
          account: account,
          name: admin_raw[:name],
          email: admin_raw[:email],
          password: admin_raw[:password],
          role: "admin"
        )

        account_valid = account.valid?
        user_valid = user.valid?

        unless account_valid && user_valid
          merged_errors = account.errors.to_hash(true)
          user.errors.to_hash(true).each do |key, messages|
            merged_errors[:"admin.#{key}"] = messages
          end
          all_messages = account.errors.full_messages + user.errors.full_messages
          return render json: {
            error: all_messages.to_sentence,
            errors: merged_errors
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        verification_token = nil
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          account.save!
          user.save!
          account.update!(owner: user)
          verification_token = user.generate_email_verification_token!
        end

        UserMailer.email_verification(user, verification_token).deliver_now

        render json: {
          account: account.as_api_json,
          user: user.as_api_json
        }, status: :created
      end

      def show
        render json: { account: current_account.as_api_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def cancel
        if current_account.cancelled?
          return render json: { error: "Account is already cancelled" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        current_account.cancel!
        render json: { account: current_account.as_api_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def reactivate
        unless current_account.cancelled?
          return render json: { error: "Account is not cancelled" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        unless current_account.reactivable?
          return render json: { error: "Account reactivation window has expired" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        current_account.reactivate!
        render json: { account: current_account.as_api_json }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end

class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  class InvalidDeliveryError < StandardError; end

  LIST_HEADERS = %i[
    list_id
    list_unsubscribe
    list_subscribe
    list_post
    list_help
    list_owner
    list_archive
    mailing_list
    x_mailing_list
    x_beenthere
    x_loop
  ].freeze

  AUTOMATED_LOCAL_PARTS = /\A(?:mailer-daemon|postmaster|no-?reply|do-?not-?reply)\z/i

  def process
    parsed_mail = safe_parse_mail
    return bounce_invalid! unless parsed_mail

    message_id = inbound_email.message_id.to_s.strip
    return bounce_invalid! if message_id.blank? || message_id.include?("\u0000")

    return if InboundEmailReceipt.exists?(message_id: message_id)

    return bounce_invalid! if automated_or_list_headers?(parsed_mail)

    sender_address = safe_from_address(parsed_mail)
    sender_email = sender_address&.address.to_s.strip.downcase
    return bounce_invalid! unless valid_sender_email?(sender_email)

    support_domain = SupportEmail.domain
    return bounce_invalid! if sender_email.end_with?("@#{support_domain}")
    return bounce_invalid! if automated_sender_address?(sender_email)

    recipient_emails = extract_recipient_emails(parsed_mail)
    destination = resolve_destination(recipient_emails, support_domain)
    return bounce_invalid! unless destination

    plain_body = sanitize_text(extract_plain_text_body(parsed_mail))
    return bounce_invalid! if plain_body.nil?

    has_message_id_header = explicit_message_id_present?(parsed_mail)

    case destination[:mode]
    when :reply
      process_reply(
        account: destination[:account],
        ticket: destination[:ticket],
        sender_email: sender_email,
        plain_body: plain_body,
        message_id: message_id,
        has_message_id_header: has_message_id_header
      )
    when :new_ticket
      subject = sanitize_text(safe_subject(parsed_mail))
      return bounce_invalid! if subject.nil?

      process_new_ticket(
        account: destination[:account],
        sender_address: sender_address,
        sender_email: sender_email,
        subject: subject,
        plain_body: plain_body,
        message_id: message_id,
        has_message_id_header: has_message_id_header
      )
    else

    end
  end

  private

  def bounce_invalid!

  end

  def safe_parse_mail

  def process_reply(account:, ticket:, sender_email:, plain_body:, message_id:, has_message_id_header:)
    requester = ticket.requester
    unless requester && requester.customer? && !requester.suspended? && requester.email.casecmp?(sender_email)
      return bounce_invalid!

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      account.lock!
      raise InvalidDeliveryError if account.reload.cancelled?

      return if InboundEmailReceipt.exists?(message_id: message_id)

      ticket.lock!
      requester.reload
      unless requester.customer? && !requester.suspended? && requester.email.casecmp?(sender_email)
        raise InvalidDeliveryError

      comment = Comment.new(
        account: account,
        ticket: ticket,
        author: requester,
        body: plain_body,
        public: true

      raise InvalidDeliveryError unless comment.valid?

      now = Time.current
      ticket.status = "open" if ticket.status.in?(%w[pending solved])
      raise InvalidDeliveryError unless ticket.valid?

      comment.save!
      ticket.updated_at = now
      ticket.customer_updated_at = now
      ticket.save!

      InboundEmailReceipt.create!(
        account: account,
        ticket: ticket,
        comment: comment,
        message_id: message_id,
        has_message_id_header: has_message_id_header

    matched_accounts = []
    matched_tickets = []
    plain_addressed = false

    support_recipients.each do |local_part|
      if local_part.include?("+")
        subdomain_part, _, token_part = local_part.partition("+")
        return nil if subdomain_part.blank? || token_part.blank?

        target_subdomains << subdomain_part
        account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain_part)

        matched_accounts << account
        matched_tickets << ticket

        matched_accounts << account if account
        plain_addressed = true
      end

    return nil unless target_subdomains.uniq.size == 1 && unique_accounts.size == 1

    account = unique_accounts.first
    return nil if account.cancelled?

    unique_tickets = matched_tickets.uniq(&:id)
    return nil if unique_tickets.size > 1

    return true if parsed_mail.mime_type&.downcase == "multipart/report"

    header_values(parsed_mail, :auto_submitted).each do |val|
      token = val.split(";").first.to_s.strip.downcase
      return true if token.present? && token != "no"

      token = val.split(";").first.to_s.strip.downcase
      return true if BULK_PRECEDENCES.include?(token)
    end

      return true if header_values(parsed_mail, header_name).any? { |v| v.strip.present? }
    end

    return true if header_values(parsed_mail, :x_auto_response_suppress).any? { |v| v.strip.present? }

    %i[x_autoreply x_autorespond].each do |header_name|
      header_values(parsed_mail, header_name).each do |val|
        normalized = val.strip.downcase
        return true if normalized.present? && !%w[no false 0].include?(normalized)
      end
    end

    header_values(parsed_mail, :return_path).each do |val|
      return true if val.strip == "<>"
    end

    false
  end

    local_part = sender_email.rpartition("@").first
    local_part.match?(AUTOMATED_LOCAL_PARTS)
  end

  def header_values(parsed_mail, name)
    fields = parsed_mail.header[name]
    return [] if fields.nil?

    Array(fields).filter_map do |field|
      (field.respond_to?(:decoded) ? field.decoded : field.to_s).to_s
    rescue StandardError
      field.to_s rescue nil
    end
  end

  def safe_from_address(parsed_mail)
    parsed_mail.from_address
  rescue StandardError
    raw = header_values(parsed_mail, :from).first
    raw.present? ? (Mail::Address.new(raw) rescue nil) : nil
  end

  def valid_sender_email?(email)
    email.present? && !email.include?("\u0000") && email.match?(URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP)
  end

  def extract_sender_name(sender_address, sender_email)
    raw_name = begin
      sender_address&.display_name
    rescue StandardError
      nil
    end
    cleaned = sanitize_utf8(raw_name.to_s).delete("\u0000").strip
    return cleaned if cleaned.present?

    sender_email.rpartition("@").first.presence || sender_email
  end

  def extract_recipient_emails(parsed_mail)
    emails = []

    %i[to cc bcc].each do |field_name|
      begin
        addrs = parsed_mail.public_send("#{field_name}_addresses")
        emails.concat(Array(addrs).filter_map(&:address))
      rescue StandardError
        emails.concat(scan_emails_from_headers(parsed_mail, field_name))
      end
    end

    %i[x_original_to x_forwarded_to delivered_to].each do |field_name|
      emails.concat(scan_emails_from_headers(parsed_mail, field_name))
    end

    emails
      .filter_map { |addr| addr.to_s.strip.downcase.presence }
      .reject { |addr| addr.include?("\u0000") }
      .uniq
  end

  def scan_emails_from_headers(parsed_mail, field_name)
    header_values(parsed_mail, field_name).flat_map do |val|
      list = Mail::AddressList.new(val)
      list.addresses.filter_map(&:address)
    rescue StandardError
      val.scan(/[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}/i)
    end
  end

  def safe_subject(parsed_mail)
    raw = parsed_mail.subject
    return nil if raw.nil?

    sanitize_utf8(raw.to_s)
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def extract_plain_text_body(part)
    if part.multipart?
      part.parts.each do |subpart|
        next if attachment_part?(subpart)

        found = extract_plain_text_body(subpart)
        return found unless found.nil?
      end
      nil
    else
      return nil if attachment_part?(part)

      mime = part.mime_type&.downcase
      if mime.nil? || mime == "text/plain"
        decode_text_part(part)
      end
    end
  end

  def attachment_part?(part)
    part.attachment?
  rescue StandardError
    false
  end

  def decode_text_part(part)
    raw = part.decoded
    return nil if raw.nil?

    charset = part.charset.presence
    str = if raw.encoding == Encoding::UTF_8 && raw.valid_encoding?
      raw
    elsif charset
      begin
        raw.dup.force_encoding(Encoding.find(charset)).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
      rescue ArgumentError, EncodingError
        sanitize_utf8(raw)
      end
    else
      sanitize_utf8(raw)
    end

    str.gsub("\r\n", "\n").gsub("\r", "\n")
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def sanitize_utf8(str)
    utf8 = str.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
    return utf8 if utf8.valid_encoding?

    str.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::ISO_8859_1).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
  end

  def sanitize_text(str)
    return nil if str.nil? || str.include?("\u0000")

    stripped = str.strip
    stripped.present? ? str : nil
  end

  def explicit_message_id_present?(parsed_mail)
    raw = parsed_mail.header[:message_id]&.unparsed_value.to_s.strip
    raw.present? && raw != "<>"
  rescue StandardError
    false
  end
end

Okay, so I've got this email subject line, and I need to parse it, right? It's straightforward enough to pull that apart, nothing complicated there. But wait a minute, the real question I need to answer is about handling `Message-ID` effectively within ActionMailbox. It's time to dig into this.

Specifically, I need to compare `ActionMailbox::TestHelper`'s `receive_inbound_email_from_mail` approach in unit tests with the `POST /rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` endpoint, often used for integration tests. The core thing I'm worried about here is the extraction of the `Message-ID`.

I've been looking at the `config/initializers/action_mailbox.rb` file and the `extract_message_id(source)` method, and I see a potential area for improvement here. Right now, it doesn't handle different casing of the domain part of the Message-ID. So I need to normalize domain case in the `Message-ID`. The plan is to update the `extract_message_id` method to do that; something like this: I'll split the id into the local, separator and domain, then convert the domain to lowercase.

The real test is if a `Message-ID` like `<msg-1@Example.TEST>` shows up *before* a `<msg-1@example.test>` arrives. If that happens, after my change, both should resolve to `"msg-1@example.test"` and deduplication should work as expected. No matter the incoming order, the system must properly identify and deduplicate emails.

I'm feeling confident about this, so I will update `config/initializers/action_mailbox.rb` with this domain-case normalization, and then, most importantly, I'm going to create a **thorough** test suite that addresses *every* possible requirement and edge case I can think of. cat <<'EOF' > /app/config/initializers/action_mailbox.rb
module Helpdesk
  module InboundEmailExtensions
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    def route_later
      if Rails.env.test?
        ActionMailbox::RoutingJob.perform_now(self)
      else
        super
      end
    end

    module ClassMethods
      def create_and_extract_message_id!(source, **options)
        message_checksum = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(source)
        message_id = extract_message_id(source) || generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)

        if (existing = find_by(message_id: message_id, message_checksum: message_checksum))
          if (existing.bounced? || existing.failed?) && !InboundEmailReceipt.exists?(message_id: message_id)
            existing.incinerate
          else
            return nil
          end
        end

        create! raw_email: create_and_upload_raw_email!(source),
          message_id: message_id, message_checksum: message_checksum, **options
      rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
        nil
      end

      private

      def extract_message_id(source)
        mail = Mail.from_source(source)
        raw_unparsed = mail.header[:message_id]&.unparsed_value
        return nil if raw_unparsed.nil?

        stripped_raw = raw_unparsed.to_s.strip
        return nil if stripped_raw.empty? || stripped_raw == "<>"

        parsed = mail.message_id.to_s.strip.gsub(/\A<+|>+\z/, "").strip
        return nil if parsed.empty? || parsed.include?("\u0000")

        if parsed.include?("@")
          local_part, _, domain_part = parsed.rpartition("@")
          parsed = "#{local_part}@#{domain_part.downcase}" if local_part.present? && domain_part.present?
        end

        parsed
      rescue StandardError
        nil
      end
    end
  end
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_mailbox_inbound_email) do
  prepend Helpdesk::InboundEmailExtensions
  singleton_class.prepend Helpdesk::InboundEmailExtensions::ClassMethods
end

**Integration Test Planning for Email Support and Replies**

Okay, so I need to create a rock-solid integration test suite, `test/integration/email_support_and_replies_test.rb`, to cover all the bases for email support and reply functionality. It's crucial this is an exhaustive test, because email processing is complex and error-prone. We're also using a live HTTP Puma test to verify the real out-of-process HTTP relay ingress within `RAILS_ENV=test`.

Here’s the breakdown of my testing plan:

1.  **Ingress Authentication and Processing:** I’ll confirm that the system correctly handles various authentication scenarios (missing auth, incorrect credentials, wrong content type, and the correct auth with the right content type) and that valid messages are processed synchronously, immediately creating tickets and comments.

2.  **Support Domain Configuration:** I will need to verify both the default support domain (`support.example.test`) and a custom one (e.g., `inbound.custom-helpdesk.test`), ensuring correct email routing and that staff reply addresses are correctly constructed.

3.  **Ticket Creation from Email:** I'll check that a new ticket is opened from emails, verifying the use of plain text email bodies (ignoring HTML) and that subject and body decoding handles things like UTF-8 and quoted-printable correctly.

4.  **Business Identification from Recipients:** I need to make sure the system can correctly identify the correct business based on the `To:` and `Cc:` fields, including handling case-insensitive addresses. I need to make sure that scenarios with multiple businesses, unknown businesses, or canceled businesses are properly handled, meaning no tickets are created for them.

5.  **Customer Management and Verification:** I will need to test customer creation, verification, and reuse. This includes new customers, existing verified and unverified customers, and cross-business scenarios. I'll need to confirm that verification emails are sent and that customers can sign in after verification and see their tickets. I will also need to verify that verification is only requested on a new user, and not re-requested on a second attempt by an unverified user.

6.  **Staff Replies and Notes:** I'll test how staff replies and notes are handled. Specifically, I'll need to check how public replies to email-origin tickets work (emails are sent), how private notes work (no email sent), and what happens when only the status or assignment is updated (no email). I need to make sure that a public response on a portal-origin ticket does *not* send out an email.

7.  **Customer Replies and Ticket Reopening:** I need to verify that customers can reply to email-origin tickets using private reply addresses, even if there are multiple tickets open. I need to check that only the requester can reply, and that replies correctly reopen `pending` or `solved` tickets. I need to test that a new message to the plain support address (without the private reply address) *always* opens a new ticket, even if there's an existing thread.

8.  **Deduplication and Retry Handling:** This is critical. I'll need to verify that duplicate emails (same `Message-ID`) are deduplicated (only one ticket, one comment, etc.). I need to test that redeliveries with the *same* `Message-ID`, even with modified headers, are deduplicated. I need to make sure that invalid deliveries don't block subsequent valid retries using the same `Message-ID`. I will need to test several scenarios: empty body/blank subject retries, cancelled/suspended account retries, invalid auth/content-type retries, and reply to invalid sender retries.

9.  **Ignoring Automated Mail:** I'll need to make sure that automated messages (auto-replies, mailing list messages, etc.) are correctly ignored, following RFC guidelines and checking various headers and fields, while still handling normal human mail.

10. **Account Purge Cleanup:** Finally, I must confirm that account purge operations (`Account.purge_cancelled!`) correctly remove all related data (tickets, comments, receipts) without causing any foreign key errors, ensuring data consistency.

And to make sure we leave no stone unturned, we'll run `bin/ci` as part of this process too, to ensure we are testing the entire CI pipeline.

But this isn't enough, I want absolute certainty about the synchronous ticket creation. So, let's get even more direct. Let's run a specific Puma test script *right now*. I want to make certain that the out-of-process HTTP client hitting `http://127.0.0.1:3099/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` in `RAILS_ENV=test` gets the intended synchronous ticket creation when using the `ActionMailbox::Relayer` without a separate worker. cd /app && RAILS_ENV=test RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD=live-pass bundle exec puma -b tcp://127.0.0.1:3099 >/tmp/puma_test.log 2>&1 &
PUMA_PID=$!
trap "kill $PUMA_PID 2>/dev/null || true; wait $PUMA_PID 2>/dev/null || true" EXIT

for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3099/up >/dev/null; then break; fi
  sleep 0.2
done

RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails runner '
require "action_mailbox/relayer"

Account.destroy_all
ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.destroy_all

acct = Account.create!(name: "LiveTest", subdomain: "livetest")
relayer = ActionMailbox::Relayer.new(
  url: "http://127.0.0.1:3099/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails",
  password: "live-pass"
)

raw = <<~RFC822
  From: Live User <live@customer.test>
  To: livetest@support.example.test
  Message-ID: <live-1@customer.test>
  Subject: Live Puma Test

  Hello from live HTTP relay!
RFC822

res = relayer.relay(raw)
raise "Relay failed: #{res.inspect}" unless res.success?
raise "Expected 1 ticket immediately, got #{acct.tickets.count}" unless acct.tickets.count == 1
raise "Wrong subject" unless acct.tickets.first.subject == "Live Puma Test"
raise "Wrong comment" unless acct.tickets.first.comments.first.body == "Hello from live HTTP relay!"

puts "LIVE PUMA RELAY VERIFIED SUCCESSFULLY!"

Account.destroy_all
ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.destroy_all
'
rm -f /tmp/puma_test.log

steps.message:
Email support and email reply threading have been implemented with Action Mailbox:

- **Action Mailbox & Relay Ingress**:
  - Configured `config.action_mailbox.ingress = :relay` at `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, authenticated with `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`, and installed the Active Storage and Action Mailbox migrations.
  - Configured `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail#route_later` in `test` to execute `ActionMailbox::RoutingJob.perform_now(self)` synchronously before the request completes so no separate worker is needed.
- **Support Domain, Recipient Resolution & Customer Handling (`SupportMailbox` & `SupportEmail`)**:
  - Resolves businesses at `<subdomain>@<HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN>` (default `support.example.test`) across recipients including `To` and `Cc`, ignoring mail addressed to multiple businesses, unknown/cancelled businesses, or automated/list headers (`Auto-Submitted`, `Precedence`, `List-*`, `X-Auto-Response-Suppress`, `Return-Path: <>`, `multipart/report`, daemon/noreply senders).
  - Opens an email-origin ticket (`email_origin: true`, `status: "open"`) with the email's subject and plain-text message as the initial public comment.
  - Reuses existing customers without verifying their account, or creates an unverified customer and sends a verification email via `UserMailer#email_verification` so they can later verify and use the portal.
- **Outbound Staff Replies & Private Ticket Reply Addresses (`TicketMailer`, `Ticket`, `TicketsController`)**:
  - Generates a unique private reply token per ticket (`<subdomain>+<reply_token>@<HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN>`).
  - Emails public staff replies on email-origin tickets to the requester with the ticket's private reply address and threading headers (`In-Reply-To`, `References`).
  - Accepts email replies only from the ticket's requester, reopens `pending` or `solved` tickets to `open`, and opens a new ticket when a message is sent to the plain support address.
- **Message-ID Deduplication & Retry Safety (`InboundEmailReceipt` & `InboundEmailExtensions`)**:
  - Deduplicates valid deliveries by `Message-ID` while ensuring invalid/rejected deliveries do not record a receipt or block later valid retries.
